requirements.quote: QUIC versions are identified using a 32-bit unsigned number.
requirements.condition: When representing or processing a QUIC version identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the version identifier as a 32-bit unsigned number.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a value outside the unsigned 32-bit range for a QUIC version identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The width and unsigned numeric domain of the version field can be checked in declarations, encoders, decoders, and boundary tests.

requirements.quote: The version 0x00000000 is reserved to represent version negotiation.
requirements.condition: When the version field has value 0x00000000.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the value as representing version negotiation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not treat 0x00000000 as an ordinary protocol version.
requirements.why_checkable: A focused parser or packet-processing test can verify the fixed value's reserved meaning and dispatch behavior.

requirements.quote:
This version of the specification is identified by the number
   0x00000001.
requirements.condition: When identifying the QUIC version defined by this specification.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's supported version constant and encoded version field can be compared with the fixed value.

requirements.quote:
Version 0x00000001 of QUIC uses TLS as a cryptographic handshake
   protocol, as described in [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When performing the cryptographic handshake for QUIC version 0x00000001.
requirements.required_behavior: Use TLS as the cryptographic handshake protocol.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake selection for version 0x00000001 can be inspected statically and exercised in an interoperability test.

requirements.quote:
Versions with the most significant 16 bits of the version number
   cleared are reserved for use in future IETF consensus documents.
requirements.condition: When a version number has its most significant 16 bits cleared.
requirements.required_behavior: Classify the version number as reserved.
requirements.why_checkable: The bit-pattern predicate and resulting reserved classification can be tested across matching and nonmatching values.

requirements.quote:
Versions that follow the pattern 0x?a?a?a?a are reserved for use in
   forcing version negotiation to be exercised -- that is, any version
   number where the low four bits of all bytes is 1010 (in binary).  A
   client or server MAY advertise support for any of these reserved
   versions.
requirements.condition: When every byte of a version number has low four bits equal to binary 1010.
requirements.required_behavior: Classify the version number as reserved for exercising version negotiation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not classify a version matching 0x?a?a?a?a as a real protocol version.
requirements.why_checkable: A mask-based test can enumerate matching values and verify their reserved classification.

requirements.quote:
Versions that follow the pattern 0x?a?a?a?a are reserved for use in
   forcing version negotiation to be exercised -- that is, any version
   number where the low four bits of all bytes is 1010 (in binary).  A
   client or server MAY advertise support for any of these reserved
   versions.
requirements.condition: When a client or server constructs a supported-version advertisement.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit advertising support for a reserved version matching 0x?a?a?a?a.
requirements.why_checkable: Configuration and advertisement-generation tests can verify that the implementation accepts and emits such a reserved value.

requirements.quote: Reserved version numbers will never represent a real protocol; a
requirements.condition: When processing any reserved version number.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the number as reserved rather than as a real protocol version.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not associate a reserved version number with a real protocol implementation.
requirements.why_checkable: Static version tables and runtime dispatch tests can verify that no reserved value selects a real protocol handler.

requirements.quote:
client MAY use one of these version numbers with the expectation that
   the server will initiate version negotiation; a server MAY advertise
   support for one of these versions and can expect that clients ignore
   the value.
requirements.condition: When a client sends one of the reserved version numbers described by the preceding pattern.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the client to use that reserved version number to cause the server to initiate version negotiation.
requirements.why_checkable: A client configuration and packet-generation test can verify that use of the reserved value is allowed and produces the intended version-negotiation stimulus.

requirements.quote:
client MAY use one of these version numbers with the expectation that
   the server will initiate version negotiation; a server MAY advertise
   support for one of these versions and can expect that clients ignore
   the value.
requirements.condition: When a server advertises supported versions.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the server to advertise support for one of the reserved version numbers.
requirements.why_checkable: A server advertisement-generation test can verify that a reserved version is accepted and encoded in the advertised list.

requirements.quote:
client MAY use one of these version numbers with the expectation that
   the server will initiate version negotiation; a server MAY advertise
   support for one of these versions and can expect that clients ignore
   the value.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a server advertisement containing one of these reserved version numbers.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not select or attempt to use the advertised reserved value as a real protocol version.
requirements.why_checkable: A client test can inject an advertisement containing a reserved value and verify that it is excluded from version selection.
